cohort: The study included live births from low-risk women with non-anomalous singleton gestations who delivered at 37-41 weeks, where a 10-minute Apgar score was documented due to an abnormal 5-minute Apgar score (0-5).
finding: Newborn infants with a lower 10-minute Apgar score were associated with a significantly higher risk of composite neonatal adverse outcomes and infant mortality among low-risk pregnancies.
